objective: Proof and computation. Orient every cut of a knot space's splice tree from its point side to its line side. Removing a line M holds every cut whose point side avoids M and opens every cut whose point side contains M. Beyond a held cut nothing depends on M: the far point side keeps exactly the knots of its own contraction without its closing line. Beyond an opened cut M acts only through the interface, which is the set of patterns the near contraction allows on the closing line once M is gone. Checked on chains and trees of three and four pieces.
status: Proved by SPLICE-TREE-20261102-001A-P001: in a knot space assembled along a tree of simple 3-edge cuts, removing a line holds every cut pointing toward it (ports tied; the far point side keeps exactly its own system's circuits, whatever was removed) and opens every cut pointing away from it (port patterns exactly those the near contraction allows without the removed line). Checked on six chains and trees of three and four pieces (107 held, 69 opened)
title: A removal opens exactly the cuts that point away from it
